mutants.expected_detection: Exhaustive/directed testbench vectors with mode=11 across all data_in/amount/direction combinations will observe data_out driven to 8'bx (or non-reference values after 4-state resolution) whereas the reference netlist deterministically resolves mode=11 to the logical-shift datapath; comparison against the simulated reference netlist fails on every mode=11 vector.

Testbench vectors with mode=01, direction=0 (left shift), data_in[7]=1, across all amount values will show data_out sign-extended into low bits instead of zero-filled, diverging from the reference netlist's logical-left-shift behavior (n3), causing functional_equivalence and mode-specific comparison to fail on these vectors.

Exhaustive/dense testbench vectors with mode=00, direction=0 (logical left shift) across amount=0..7 will mismatch against the reference netlist's simulated data_out whenever amount>0, since the submission shifts by amount+1 instead of amount, causing bit-exact comparison failures for the vast majority of mode=00 left-shift vectors (and cascades into mode=01 left-shift and mode=11 don't-care resolution since they reuse logical_res).

Exhaustive vectors with mode=01: for direction=1 (right) the output will use the stale/incorrect default `result` value (from the case statement's fallthrough of logical_res via arith_res always evaluating logical_res regardless of direction) instead of the true arithmetic right shift sign-extended result, causing mismatches against the reference netlist for any data_in with MSB=1 and amount>0 under mode=01, direction=1 -- detected by functional_equivalence and the mode=01 targeted vectors.

Exhaustive vectors under mode=10 (rotate) with direction=0 and direction=1 across all amount 0-7 and data_in values will show data_out mismatches against the reference netlist's rl3/rr3 datapaths, since the mutant swaps which rotate direction each direction value selects (direction=0 now yields rotate-right behavior and direction=1 yields rotate-left behavior), causing FR3 functional_equivalence and mode-specific checks to fail for nearly all rotate vectors with amount != 0.

Exhaustive vector comparison against the simulated reference netlist under mode=10 (rotate) for amount values 5,6,7 will reveal that data_out no longer matches the netlist's rotate datapath, since the recovered RTL now masks amount to only 2 bits (amount % 4) before rotating instead of using the full 3-bit amount (mod 8), causing wrong results for amount>=4 in both rotate directions and breaking bit-exact combinational equivalence required by FR4.
